name: Ferrogate Deep Line
description: The subway lines that descend below the standard metro level into the Underworld. The first three levels are official Ferrogate routes with functioning stations and lighting. Below Level 3, the tunnels continue — unmaintained, unmapped, and officially nonexistent. The trains that run down there aren't on any schedule. Some say they're automated ghosts running loops from before the city was built. Others say someone is driving them.
speed: 35 km/h on maintained track, variable below
cost: Φ3 per ride (upper levels), free if you can find the deep platforms
autonomy: Automated dispatch on upper levels. Deep level trains operate independently.
armament: None officially. Deep level trains have been observed with reinforced plating.
common_usage: Upper levels: standard commute for underground district workers. Deep levels: smugglers, refugees, the desperate, and the curious who don't come back.
story_hooks: A Deep Line train arrives at a Level 2 station covered in frost — the doors open and no one is inside
Someone maps the deep rail network and realizes the tunnels form a pattern that predates the city
physical_description: Massive iron-ribbed tunnel infrastructure descends in concentric circles, with rusted steel support beams and concrete walls slick with mineral seepage and bioluminescent algae bloom. Upper levels gleam with faded Ferrogate signage and flickering sodium-vapor fixtures, while lower sections deteriorate into bare stone and corroded rail lines that disappear into absolute darkness, the metal worn smooth by decades of unseen transit.
